text: Lesson 3 already set up this comparison: Managed Instance trades a little PaaS convenience for near-complete SQL Server surface area. Migrating into it proves that out — the parity gaps from last lesson mostly disappear here.

Cross-database queries work, because Managed Instance hosts multiple databases under one instance like on-prem. SQL Server Agent is native, not Elastic Jobs. Linked servers, CLR, and Service Broker are supported — exactly the dependencies that would have blocked a move to Azure SQL Database.

This is the one thing Azure SQL Database cannot do at all: back up on-prem straight to a storage account URL, then restore on Managed Instance from that same URL. Same BACKUP and RESTORE syntax, just pointed at blob storage instead of local disk.

Higher parity doesn't mean zero friction: migration time, since restoring a large backup from blob storage can take hours; network requirements, since Managed Instance lives inside a VNet; and instance sizing done before cutover, not reactively after go-live.
Same BACKUP and RESTORE skill from Chapter 13, just aimed at a URL instead of a disk path. Next up: post-migration validation, and what to do when a migration goes wrong.
